verses.1: Rejoice in the LORD, you upright ones. It is good for those who are righteous to praise.
verses.2: Give thanks to the LORD with the lyre, with a ten-stringed harp, sing to him.
verses.3: Sing to him a new song, play skillfully with a loud sound.
verses.4: For the word of the LORD is upright, and all his works are in faithfulness.
verses.5: He loves righteousness and judgment. The steadfast love of the LORD fills the earth.
verses.6: By the word of the LORD the heavens were made, and by the breath of his mouth all their host.
verses.7: He gathers the waters of the sea as a heap, and puts the depths into storehouses.
verses.8: Let all the earth fear the LORD, and let all the inhabitants of the world tremble before him.
verses.9: For he spoke, and it came to be; he commanded, and it stood firm.
verses.10: The LORD frustrates the counsel of the nations; he nullifies the plans of the peoples.
verses.11: The counsel of the LORD stands forever, the thoughts of his heart through all generations.
verses.12: Happy is the nation whose God is the LORD, the people he has chosen as his heritage.
verses.13: From heaven the LORD looks, he sees all the children of humanity.
verses.14: From the place of his dwelling he looks out over all the inhabitants of the earth.
verses.15: The one who fashions their hearts together, the one who understands all their works.
verses.16: A king is not saved by a great army, a warrior is not delivered by great strength.
verses.17: A horse is a false hope for rescue, in the abundance of its strength it cannot be saved.
verses.18: Behold, the eyes of the LORD are on those who fear him, on those who wait for his steadfast love.
verses.19: To deliver their lives from death, and to keep them alive in famine.
verses.20: Our soul has waited for the LORD, he is our help and our shield.
verses.21: For in him our heart rejoices, because we trust in his holy name.
verses.22: Let your steadfast love, LORD, be upon us, just as we have hoped in you.

notes:
Notes
- v. 5: "steadfast love" reflects חסד, a central theological term.
- v. 16-17: The contrast between human strength and divine faithfulness is central to the psalm’s message; the rendering follows the literal Hebrew but preserves the thematic contrast.

[2] Give thanks to the LORD with the lyre, with a ten-stringed harp, sing to him.

[3] Sing to him a new song, play skillfully with a loud sound.

[9] For he spoke, and it came to be; he commanded, and it stood firm.

[10] The LORD frustrates the counsel of the nations; he nullifies the plans of the peoples.

[13] From heaven the LORD looks, he sees all the children of humanity.

[14] From the place of his dwelling he looks out over all the inhabitants of the earth.

[17] A horse is a false hope for rescue, in the abundance of its strength it cannot be saved.

[18] Behold, the eyes of the LORD are on those who fear him, on those who wait for his steadfast love.

[19] To deliver their lives from death, and to keep them alive in famine.

[20] Our soul has waited for the LORD, he is our help and our shield.

[21] For in him our heart rejoices, because we trust in his holy name.

[22] Let your steadfast love, LORD, be upon us, just as we have hoped in you.
